prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() skips pre-parsing for ANY union whose members are all in {str,int,float,bool,None} - this also disables pre-parsing for `str | int`, `str | float`, and `str | bool` params, removing the existing numeric/bool string-coercion behavior for those annotations, which is a behavior change beyond the reported corruption bug. It also decides membership via `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES`, which fails for a union member wrapped in `Annotated[...]` (e.g. `str | Annotated[str, Field(...)]`), incorrectly falling back to pre-parse=True in that case. #3056's _is_optional_str() targets only `str | None`, the one union shape where a successful json.loads() can never legitimately produce a value matching the annotation (a decoded int/float/bool/list/dict never satisfies `str | None`), so it fixes the exact reported corruption with no side effects on other coercions, and it explicitly unwraps `Annotated` on each union member before checking, covering the case #2032 misses.

clusters.pick_reason: #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() skips pre-parsing for ANY union whose members are all in {str,int,float,bool,None} - this also disables pre-parsing for `str | int`, `str | float`, and `str | bool` params, removing the existing numeric/bool string-coercion behavior for those annotations, which is a behavior change beyond the reported corruption bug. It also decides membership via `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES`, which fails for a union member wrapped in `Annotated[...]` (e.g. `str | Annotated[str, Field(...)]`), incorrectly falling back to pre-parse=True in that case. #3056's _is_optional_str() targets only `str | None`, the one union shape where a successful json.loads() can never legitimately produce a value matching the annotation (a decoded int/float/bool/list/dict never satisfies `str | None`), so it fixes the exact reported corruption with no side effects on other coercions, and it explicitly unwraps `Annotated` on each union member before checking, covering the case #2032 misses.

As shown, #2478 does not appear to actually override pickling behavior, so it likely does not resolve the TypeError that #2555 demonstrably fixes with a test.

members.cluster_pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` by `str(request_id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC's distinct int and string ids (e.g. `1` and `"1"`) into the same key — causing false 409s across differently-typed ids and leaving a residual cross-wiring risk — and doesn't guard against a string id colliding with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel. #3221 introduces a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (`i:`/`s:` prefixes) that fixes both edge cases while implementing the same duplicate-id rejection, making it a strict superset of #3063's fix.
